summary: Transfers & controlled resale — carved out of TKT-9, blocked on an open product decision
description:
Carved out of TKT-9 at decomposition (2026-07-31). The epic's prose lists *transfers and controlled resale* alongside refunds/exchanges/cancellation, but it is **not** in the epic's Conditions of Success, and it is not buildable today:

1. **Open product decision.** `docs/product/prd-v1.md` lists *resale marketplace rules (TKT-9)* in its own open-decisions section. Nobody has decided the rules — price caps, who may resell, fee treatment, whether resale is peer-to-peer or organizer-brokered. Building against an undecided rule set is how you ship the wrong thing twice.
2. **Missing prerequisite.** The PRD names customer accounts (TKT-21, *'guest checkout + optional account, ticket wallet, prerequisites for transfers/limits'*) as the prerequisite for transfers. Today's checkout is guest-only with a `guest_order_ref`; there is no account to transfer a ticket **to**.

The trail already anticipates both: ADR-003 names `transferred` and `resold` among the ticket lifecycle states, so this lands as lifecycle events when it lands.

**Not ready. Do not prioritize** until the resale rules are decided and TKT-21 exists. Shaping this ticket starts with a decision, not a plan.

binding.rule: every ticket/entitlement state change (issued, delivered, transferred, resold, exchanged, redeemed, reissued, invalidated) is an append-only lifecycle event linked to its order.

governingAdrs.why: Every lifecycle event goes through store.appendLifecycle — the verifier asserts one-to-one coverage, so a direct INSERT into lifecycle_events reads as tampering and fails `access verify-lifecycle` in the gate. Canonical forms are pinned by golden literals; changing a byte is a canonical-version migration, not a test update. Also: name the adversary before writing 'tamper-evident'.

Corrections are COMPENSATING ENTRIES, never mutations. A refund/exchange appends a new signed fact; the original sale fact and its hash link are untouched. The payments journal has a DB trigger that raises on UPDATE/DELETE — any design that 'adjusts' a fact is rejected by the database, not by review.

objective.note: Tracks the carved-out half of TKT-9's prose so it is not silently lost when the epic closes on its COS.

scope.note: Undefined until the resale rules are decided.

uncertainties.note: The whole ticket is the uncertainty: resale rules are an open product decision.

context_memo.note: Minimal mémo baked: the lifecycle-trail constraint that will govern it whenever it runs.

### ❌ Implementation readiness — FAIL (deliberately)

Not a defect: this ticket exists to *hold* scope that cannot be shaped yet. Four DoR items are `open` and the board will refuse Gate 1 until the resale rules are decided and TKT-21 lands. That refusal is the point.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### One of two blockers discharged — **still hold at Gate 1**

Backlog review 2026-08-25 at HEAD `ad849f98`.

**Removed the stale `blocked-by: TKT-21`.** The ticket named two blockers; this was the second of them:

> **Missing prerequisite.** The PRD names customer accounts (TKT-21 …) as the prerequisite for transfers. Today's checkout is guest-only with a `guest_order_ref`; there is no account to transfer a ticket **to**.

**TKT-21 is Done** — customer accounts and the wallet shipped, so there is now an account to transfer a ticket to. That sentence in the description is out of date and should be read as discharged.

**The first blocker is untouched, and it is the one that matters.** `docs/product/prd-v1.md:378` still lists *"resale marketplace rules (TKT-9)"* in its open-decisions line. Nobody has decided price caps, who may resell, fee treatment, or whether resale is peer-to-peer or organizer-brokered. Building against an undecided rule set is what the ticket was carved out to avoid.

**So: half-unblocked, still not ready.** Six `readiness` items remain `open`, and they cannot close before the product decision does. The next move is the owner deciding the resale rules — or explicitly parking this until they do — not a Gate 1 drag.
